title: Shapes every hlekk protocol body is built from

id.title: A local object id
id.description: An unsigned 64-bit integer as a bare decimal string, below 2^63. Relative to the database that answered.

reference.title: A reference
reference.description: A local id, or a canonical database URI, '#', and that database's own local id.

database.title: A canonical database URI
database.description: https, lowercase host as A-labels, no userinfo, no default port, no trailing slash, no query, no fragment. http only for a loopback host, for development.

typeName.title: An object or edge type name
typeName.description: A name, never the catalog's integer: integers are allocated per database and mean nothing to a caller.

cost.title: What a request was priced at

nodes.description: The upper bound on answer nodes.

cacheability.title: How much of an answer the caller may keep
cacheability.description: Stated by the responder because only the responder knows its own enforcement granularity.

refusal.title: A refused request
refusal.description: The body of any 4xx or 5xx: an RFC 9457 problem with this protocol's own members beside it. `at` is a path into the submitted request, so a caller can correct the part that was wrong instead of retrying blind. Only `error` is required, because it is the only member version 1 had.

type.description: RFC 9457. A URI naming the kind of refusal, which is what a program branches on: `https://hlekk.dev/spec/problems/` and one of malformed, vocabulary, limit, signature, forbidden, not-found, method, too-large, media-type, too-many, unavailable, fault. An identifier; nothing need be served at it.

title.description: RFC 9457. The kind, in words. The same for every refusal of one `type`.

status.description: RFC 9457. The status this body was sent with, for a reader that was handed the body alone.

detail.description: RFC 9457. What `error` says. Both are sent so that a reader of either finds it.

offset.description: For a request submitted as text, where to put the caret.

id.description: The base64url SHA-256 of the key, so an id is a fact about the key and not a claim.

key.description: The raw 32-byte public key, base64url, unpadded.

signedBy.description: A signature by the key this one replaces, over this one, so a holder of the old pin can walk forward.

retired.description: When it stopped being the current key.
